levels.label: Standard
levels.about: No hints, no timer pressure except where the mission sets one.

levels.label: Expert
levels.about: No hints, timed, and the operation picker lets you make mistakes.

missions.title: First new drug application
missions.brief: Halcyon Ridge Pharmaceuticals is ready to file its first NDA for Ostrevia (lumiravostat) tablets, 10 mg and 25 mg. You are the publisher. Build sequence 0000 end to end: complete the regional metadata, assemble Module 1 and the Modules 2–5 tree from the document library, clear the validator, and publish.
steps: Fill the US regional metadata (application number, submission type, sub-type).
Place every mandatory Module 1 item: forms in 1.1, cover letter in 1.2, administrative items in 1.3, labeling in 1.14.
Place documents into every required Module 2–5 heading, and tag the study reports in Modules 4 and 5 (one click in the builder). Watch for the two granularity decoys in the library.
Run validation until there are no High or Medium findings.
Publish sequence 0000.
hints: The cover letter is not in the library: generate it in Module 1 → Cover letter, then add it to 1.2.
Repeatable section attributes (substance, manufacturer, product) come from Project settings.
The library holds a 290-page 'complete 3.2.P' file and a one-test specification. Neither belongs in a good dossier.
Required headings show a red dot in the tree; the Dossier map shows completeness at a glance.

checks.label: No granularity decoys in the dossier

missions.title: Answer an information request
missions.brief: Sequence 0000 for Ostrevia was filed and is under review. The review team has sent an information request about the drug product. Build sequence 0001 as an amendment that answers it: a response document, an updated specification and updated stability data, each with the correct lifecycle operation.

letter.from: Office of Product Quality (fictional review team)
letter.subject: NDA 299001 — Information Request: Ostrevia (lumiravostat) tablets
body: We are reviewing the chemistry, manufacturing and controls sections of your NDA and request the following information.

1. Your drug product specification (3.2.P.5.1) sets the dissolution acceptance criterion at Q = 70% in 45 minutes. Based on the batch data in 3.2.P.5.4, tighten the criterion or justify the proposed limit. Provide the revised specification.
2. Provide the 12-month long-term and 6-month accelerated stability data for the three primary stability batches, which were not available at filing (3.2.P.8.3).
Submit your response as an amendment to this application within 10 business days.

extraDocuments.title: Response to Information Request dated Day 74
Stability Data
extraDocuments.note: Updated with 12-month long-term and 6-month accelerated data.

extraDocuments.title: Justification of Specification(s)
extraDocuments.decoyNote: Not asked for: the request offered 'tighten or justify', and you tightened.

steps: Open the Sequences tab and create sequence 0001 (sub-type: amendment).
Place Form FDA 356h and a cover letter that references the information request.
Place the response document in 1.11.1.
Drop the revised specification on 3.2.P.5.1 and choose 'replace', targeting the 0000 leaf. Same for stability data in 3.2.P.8.3.
Validate, then publish 0001.
hints: The revised documents keep the same file name; they live in a different sequence folder, so there is no clash.
Do not use 'new' for an updated document — the reviewer would then see two specifications.
Only send what was asked. The revised justification is a trap: you tightened the limit, so no new justification is needed.

Open the Consistency tab after you place the revised specification: the Quality Overall Summary still quotes the old limit. In real life the agency may ask you to align it; this mission only asks for what the letter requested.

checks.label: Nothing sent that was not asked for

missions.title: Rescue the dossier
missions.brief: A contractor handed over sequence 0000 for Ostrevia the night before the filing date. It has 25 planted defects. You have 30 minutes to find and fix as many as you can before you submit it for scoring.
steps: Run the validator to see what it can find.
Fix each defect in place: rename files, edit titles, move documents, fix PDF properties, add missing items.
Re-validate as you go. Submit for scoring when you are done or when the clock runs out.
hints: Defects span every rule family: metadata, file names, PDF settings, misplaced documents, lifecycle, missing Module 1 items and granularity.
Some defects hide inside documents: open the properties panel for each flagged leaf.
Moving a document to the right heading fixes a misplacement; fixing it does not need a new sequence because 0000 is not yet published.

missions.title: Centralised marketing authorisation
missions.brief: Halcyon Ridge is filing Ostrevia (lumiravostat) tablets with the European Medicines Agency through the centralised procedure. Build sequence 0000: complete the EU envelope, assemble EU Module 1 with the eAF and QRD product information, reuse Modules 2–5, and make sure the modules agree with each other before you publish.
steps: Complete the EU envelope in Module 1: procedure tracking number EMEA/H/C/006123, procedure type, submission type maa, submission unit initial.

Place every mandatory EU Module 1 document: cover letter (1.0), eAF (1.2), product information (1.3.1), mock-ups (1.3.2), experts (1.4), ERA (1.6.1), pharmacovigilance (1.8.1, 1.8.2) and paediatrics (1.10).
Place Modules 2–5 from the library.
Open the Consistency tab and resolve every contradiction between modules.
Clear the validator and publish sequence 0000.
hints: Two library documents contradict Module 3. Look at shelf life and the drug product manufacturer's address.
In the EU, study grouping uses node extensions rather than US study tagging files, so no tagging is needed here.
EU Module 1 file names start with the country folder code, e.g. ema-cover.pdf. The generated documents already follow it.

checks.label: All mandatory EU Module 1 items placed

facts.dpManufacturer: Halcyon Ridge Manufacturing LLC, Fictionville, NY, USA

missions.title: New drug application under v4.0
missions.brief: Build submission unit 1 of the Ostrevia new drug application in Japan under eCTD v4.0: Japanese Module 1 and Module 2, the reception number, the cover, and study keywords instead of study tagging files. Publish it. Then answer the reviewers' first inquiries in unit 2 with a replacement, a suspension and a reused document.

letter.date: First inquiries, after receipt of unit 1
letter.subject: Ostrevia (lumiravostat) - first inquiries
body: Inquiry 1 (quality): Only 6 months of long-term stability data were provided. Provide the 12-month data in place of the 6-month data.
Inquiry 2 (quality): The interim photostability note in 3.2.P.8.3 is superseded by the full results in the 12-month data. It should no longer form part of the current dossier.
Inquiry 3 (clinical): The literature reference on the mechanism of action filed in 4.3 also supports the clinical discussion. Make it available in 5.4 as well, without sending it again.
Answer in unit 2 with a cover and a response document in Japanese at 1.13.3.

extraDocuments.title: Literature Reference: Mechanism of Action of Lumiravostat (J. Fict. Pharmacol. 2024)
Stability Data (12 months)
extraDocuments.note: 12-month long-term and 6-month accelerated data, including photostability.

quiz.q: What number does the first submission unit carry in eCTD v4.0?
quiz.why: v4.0 numbers submission units as positive integers starting at 1. The four-digit 0000 belongs to v3.2.2 sequences.

quiz.q: How do you take a document out of the current dossier in v4.0?
quiz.why: v4.0 has no delete or append. A context of use is replaced or suspended; the document itself stays on record.

quiz.q: A document sent in unit 1 is needed under another heading in unit 2. What is sent?
options: The file again, with a new checksum
Only a new context of use that refers to the existing document ID
A copy with a different file name
quiz.why: v4.0 separates the document from where it is used. The new context of use points to the document ID already sent, so the file is not sent again.

steps: In Module 1, enter the reception number (10 digits, e.g. 2026000123) and check the brand, JAN and applicant.

Build unit 1: Japanese Module 1 (1.1 to 1.12), the Japanese Module 2 documents (not the English ones), Modules 3 to 5, the literature reference in 4.3 and the interim photostability note in 3.2.P.8.3.
Generate the cover; it is filed as m1/jp/cover.pdf and not referenced in the XML.
Give each study report in 4.2 and 5.3 a study ID keyword (Tag studies from documents does this).
Answer the quiz, validate and publish unit 1.

In Sequences, create unit 2. Replace 3.2.P.8.3 stability data with the 12-month version, suspend the interim photostability note, place the literature reference again at 5.4 (it shows as reused), and add a cover and the response document at 1.13.3.
Validate and publish unit 2. Look at the Submission unit tab: the reused document is not in sha256.txt.
hints: Library documents marked (Japanese) are the ones to use in Module 1 and Module 2.
Suspend is offered on the earlier document's card in the builder, where v3.2.2 would offer delete.
Drag the literature reference from the library onto 5.4 in unit 2 and choose New. Because unit 1 already sent it, it becomes a reuse.

Module 1 and 2 in Japanese in unit 1
Study keywords on the study reports
Unit 2: cover and Japanese response document at 1.13.3
Unit 2 published with no High findings

missions.title: Respond to the list of questions
missions.brief: Sequence 0000 of the Ostrevia MAA is under assessment. At Day 120 the committee adopted a list of questions and the clock stopped. Build the response sequence that restarts it: a responses document, the changed Module 3 and product information, each replacing the version in 0000, with the envelope linking back to the start of the procedure.

letter.subject: EMEA/H/C/006123 - Ostrevia (lumiravostat) - List of Questions
body: Major objection 1 (quality): The proposed dissolution limit of Q = 70% in 45 minutes is not discriminating. Tighten the limit on the basis of the batch data and update the drug product specification.
Other concern 2 (clinical safety): In section 4.4 of the SmPC, add a warning on transaminase elevations observed in the pivotal studies, with corresponding package leaflet wording.
Please submit the responses within the agreed clock-stop period. The clock restarts on receipt of a valid response sequence.

missions.title: Add a new manufacturing site
missions.brief: Ostrevia is approved. Halcyon Ridge wants to add a second drug product manufacturing site, Northgate Contract Manufacturing in Pennsylvania, which has not been inspected for this product type. Decide how the change is filed in the US and how the same change would be classified in the EU, then build the US supplement.

quiz.q: How is this change filed in the US?
quiz.why: A new site that has not had a satisfactory cGMP inspection for this type of operation is a major change: it needs FDA approval before product made there can be distributed.

quiz.q: In the EU, adding a manufacturing site for a non-sterile tablet (not batch release or secondary packaging) is usually…
quiz.why: Under the variations classification guideline this is a Type IB change for non-sterile products. Sterile or biological products move to Type II.

extraDocuments.title: Form FDA 356h
extraDocuments.note: Completed for the supplement: lists both drug product sites.

steps: Answer the two classification questions in this panel.
Create sequence 0001: chemistry, manufacturing and controls supplement, sub-type application.
Place Form FDA 356h (the version completed for this supplement) and a cover letter.
Replace 3.2.P.3.1 and 3.2.A.1 with the versions that add the new site; add the new site's process validation and stability data.
Check consistency, validate and publish.
hints: The 356h in sequence 0000 lists only the original site. Use the supplement's 356h so the form agrees with 3.2.P.3.1.
The new site's validation and stability reports are additional documents: 'new' (or 'append') is right; they do not replace the original site's data.
Batch numbers for the new site differ from the original primary batches. The consistency check compares only documents about the same batches.

missions.title: Safety labelling update
missions.brief: Post-marketing surveillance of Ostrevia has identified a signal of drug-induced liver injury. The safety team wants a new Warnings and Precautions subsection on hepatotoxicity in the prescribing information without waiting for FDA approval. Classify the change and build the labeling supplement.

quiz.q: Which US filing lets the company implement a strengthened warning before FDA approval?
quiz.why: Adding or strengthening a contraindication, warning, precaution or adverse reaction can be made under a 'changes being effected' supplement and implemented on submission (21 CFR 314.70(c)(6)(iii)).

quiz.q: The equivalent safety update to the SmPC of a centrally authorised product is usually…
quiz.why: Changes to the SmPC, labelling or package leaflet driven by new safety data are generally Type II variations (category C.I.4).

extraDocuments.title: Draft Prescribing Information
extraDocuments.note: New section 5.x Hepatotoxicity; adverse reactions updated.

extraDocuments.title: Annotated Draft Labeling Text
extraDocuments.note: Annotations reference the hepatic safety review.

extraDocuments.title: Cumulative Review of Hepatic Adverse Events

steps: Answer the classification questions.
Create sequence 0001: labeling supplement, sub-type application.
Place Form FDA 356h and a cover letter.
Replace the draft labeling text (1.14.1.3) and annotated labeling (1.14.1.2), targeting their 0000 leaves.
Add the hepatic safety review in 5.3.6, validate and publish.
hints: Keep the leaf titles the same as in 0000 so reviewers recognise the replaced labeling.
The safety review is new information: operation 'new'.

missions.title: Annual report and periodic safety report
missions.brief: Ostrevia has been on the market for a year. File the first annual report, then the periodic adverse drug experience report (PADER) for the same period. Both are recurring submissions: each year's report is new, it does not replace last year's.

quiz.q: Next year, the distribution data in 1.13.11 is updated for the new reporting period. Which operation?
options: Delete last year's leaf, then new
quiz.why: Each annual report covers its own period. Last year's report stays valid as a record of that year, so the new report is filed as new documents.

extraDocuments.title: Summary of Safety Information - Reporting Period 1

steps: Answer the lifecycle question.
Create 0001: annual report, sub-type report. Place Form FDA 2252, a cover letter and the four annual report sections (1.13.3, 1.13.5, 1.13.11, 1.13.12) as new. Publish.
Create 0002: periodic safety reports, sub-type report. Place Form FDA 2252, a cover letter and the PADER (5.3.6) as new. Publish.
hints: Each report sequence needs its own Form FDA 2252 and cover letter.
In this app the PADER is placed in 5.3.6 (reports of post-marketing experience).

checks.label: 0001: annual report / report, with 2252 and cover letter
Four annual report sections placed as new

missions.title: Drug master file support
missions.brief: Corvane Fine Chemicals, the drug substance manufacturer, has amended its Type II drug master file to describe an improved final crystallisation step. Halcyon Ridge must reference the amended DMF in its NDA: an updated letter of authorization, its own summary of the process, and batch data from material made by the new step.

quiz.q: Which part of the DMF can Halcyon Ridge (the NDA holder) see?
options: Only the open (applicant's) part the holder shares
Nothing, but FDA tells it the content
quiz.why: The DMF holder keeps confidential manufacturing details in the DMF; the applicant gets the non-confidential part. The letter of authorization lets FDA read the full DMF on the applicant's behalf.

quiz.q: In the EU, the equivalent is the Active Substance Master File (ASMF). Its two parts are…
quiz.why: An ASMF has an applicant's part (shared with the MA applicant) and a restricted part (sent only to the authorities).

quiz.q: Where does the letter of authorization go in US Module 1?
quiz.why: 1.4.1 Letter of authorization.

extraDocuments.title: Letter of Authorization for DMF (Corvane Fine Chemicals)
extraDocuments.note: Updated to reference the DMF amendment of July 2026.

extraDocuments.title: Description of Manufacturing Process and Process Controls
extraDocuments.note: Applicant's summary of the revised crystallisation step; restricted details are in the DMF.

steps: Answer the three questions.
Create 0001: CMC supplement, sub-type application. Place 356h and a cover letter.
Replace the letter of authorization (1.4.1) and 3.2.S.2.2, targeting 0000.
Add the post-change batch analyses in 3.2.S.4.4 as new (or append). Validate and publish.
hints: The post-change batch data adds to, and does not replace, the original batch analyses.

missions.title: Paper to eCTD baseline
missions.brief: Ostrevia's quality dossier was originally filed as NeeS volumes. Before the next variation, the company wants an eCTD baseline: Module 3 rebuilt as granular eCTD documents in a reformat sequence, with no change in content.

Generate a cover letter (1.0) stating that the sequence is a reformat with no content change.
Rebuild 3.2.S and 3.2.P from the granular library documents. Do not use the NeeS volumes.
Leave Modules 2, 4 and 5 and the rest of Module 1 out: a baseline covers what is being reformatted.
Validate and publish 0000.
hints: The two NeeS volumes look convenient but are one file per module: far too coarse for lifecycle.
A reformat sequence must not change content, so no new product information or summaries belong in it.

checks.label: Only Module 3 and the cover letter

extraDocuments.coach: A whole-section NeeS volume. A baseline should rebuild each subsection as its own document.

missions.title: Generic application
missions.brief: Ashvale Generics is filing an ANDA for talmisartan tablets, 20 mg and 40 mg, referencing Corvenza 40 mg. Bioequivalence was shown for 40 mg under fasting and fed conditions; a biowaiver is requested for 20 mg. Choose the patent certification and build sequence 0000.

quiz.q: Corvenza has one listed patent expiring in 2031. Ashvale believes it is invalid and wants to launch before 2031. Which certification?
quiz.why: A Paragraph IV certification states the patent is invalid, unenforceable or not infringed. It triggers notice to the patent holder and possible litigation. Patent and exclusivity data come from the Orange Book (see the Orange & Purple Book Explorer app).

steps: Answer the patent certification question.
Complete the US metadata (ANDA, application number, original application / application).
Place the ANDA Module 1: forms 356h and 3794, cover letter, certifications, patent certification, basis for submission, comparison with the RLD, biowaiver request, labeling and listed drug labeling.
Place 2.3, 2.7.1, Module 3 and the bioequivalence studies in 5.3.1; tag the studies.
Clear the validator and publish.
hints: An ANDA has no Module 4 and a short Module 2: the QOS and the biopharmaceutics summary.
The BE study reports are grouped by study tagging files like any other US study.

checks.label: All mandatory ANDA Module 1 items placed
All required Module 2, 3 and 5 headings filled

missions.title: Biosimilar application
missions.brief: Build the original 351(k) biologics license application for Selvanta (olvecitamab-kzrt), a proposed biosimilar to Arventa. The library holds a document the applicant has no right to use, and the dossier has one contradiction to find. Then answer how the same product would be filed in the EU.

extraDocuments.title: Clinical Study Report: Arventa Pivotal Efficacy Study ARV-301 (reference product sponsor)
extraDocuments.note: The reference product sponsor's own study report.

quiz.q: Under which provision is a US biosimilar licensed?
quiz.why: 351(k) is the abbreviated pathway for biosimilar and interchangeable products. 351(a) is the full BLA used for Arventa itself.

quiz.q: When can FDA approve a 351(k) application at the earliest?
options: 4 years after the reference product was first licensed
12 years after the reference product was first licensed
When the reference product's patents expire, whatever the date
quiz.why: The reference product has 12 years of exclusivity from first licensure; a 351(k) application cannot be submitted until 4 years after it.

quiz.q: What is the legal basis for an EU biosimilar marketing authorisation?
quiz.why: Article 10(4) covers similar biological medicinal products: the applicant provides comparability data in place of the reference product's full non-clinical and clinical package.

quiz.q: Where does the EU Module 1 hold the information on the reference medicinal product for a biosimilar?
quiz.why: 1.5.2 is 'Information for generic, hybrid or bio-similar applications'. It identifies the reference product and summarises comparability.

steps: Set the application number (six digits) in Module 1.
Build sequence 0000: Module 1 (356h, user fee, certifications, labeling), Modules 2 to 5 with the comparative analytical, PK and efficacy studies.
Leave out anything that is not yours to file.
Open Consistency and correct the contradiction you find.
Answer the quiz, validate and publish 0000.
hints: A biosimilar applicant relies on the reference product's approval through its comparability data; it does not file the reference sponsor's reports.
Look at the potency acceptance range in Module 2 against 3.2.P.5.1.

checks.label: US and EU biosimilar questions answered correctly

missions.title: New drug application in India
missions.brief: Ostrevia is approved in the US and the EU. An Indian importer, acting as the authorised agent of the manufacturer, applies for permission to import it as a new drug. Build the CTD for the online portal with the right form, the fee receipt and the agent's documents, ask for a waiver of the local clinical trial, and get it through screening.

quiz.q: Which form is the application to import a new drug for sale or distribution?
quiz.why: Under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, CT-18 is the application to import a new drug; CT-21 is the application to manufacture one. Form 44 belongs to the older rules.

quiz.q: On what basis can the local clinical trial be waived?
options: Never: a local trial is always required
The drug is approved in a country the regulator has specified, among other conditions
The applicant pays a higher fee
quiz.why: Rule 101 lets the licensing authority, with central government approval, specify countries whose approvals can support a waiver of the local trial, subject to the conditions in the rules.

quiz.q: Within what time does the authority decide on an application for a new drug already approved outside India?
quiz.why: The rules set 90 working days for a decision on such an application.

steps: In Module 1, enter the authorised agent and the agent's address.
Check the submission type in Sequences or Module 1: import of a new drug (CT-18).

Build 0000: covering letter (1.1), the applicant introduction, CT-18 and the fee receipt (1.2.2), the agent's authorisation and the CoPP and GMP certificates (1.2.3), coordinates (1.2.4), labels (1.3), QC protocols (1.4), regulatory status and the waiver request (1.5), price (1.6), and Modules 2 to 5.
Answer the quiz, validate and publish (the CTD goes to the portal as PDF uploads; there is no backbone XML).
Open Review and send 0000 through the mock gateway. It must pass screening.
hints: The library has both CT-18 and CT-21. Only one fits an import application.
The request to waive the local clinical trial is in 1.5, with the regulatory status in other countries.

Form CT-18 and fee receipt in 1.2.2
Regulatory status and waiver request in 1.5

quiz.q: When must the renewal application be submitted?
options: At least 9 months before the authorisation expires
quiz.why: The renewal must reach the agency at least nine months before the authorisation ceases to be valid.

quiz.q: Where must the new holder of a centralised authorisation be established?
options: In the same country as the old holder
quiz.why: A marketing authorisation holder must be established in the EEA.

quiz.q: What is the related sequence for the renewal sequence?
options: None: a renewal starts a new procedure
quiz.why: The related sequence links sequences within one procedure. A renewal starts its own procedure, so it has none.

missions.title: Withdrawal
missions.brief: The Ostrevia NDA (sequence 0000) is under review. After an internal decision the company withdraws the application before action. File the withdrawal correctly: the letter in the right heading, with the dossier left exactly as it was.

letter.subject: Withdraw NDA 299001 (Ostrevia) before action
body: We will withdraw the Ostrevia NDA. Send a letter to the agency requesting withdrawal of the unapproved application, with the usual form and cover letter.
Do not change or remove anything already filed. We may refile later.

extraDocuments.title: Request for Withdrawal of Approval of an Application

quiz.q: Should the withdrawal sequence delete the documents filed in 0000?
options: Yes, every leaf, so the dossier is empty
No: the record stays as filed; the letter asks for withdrawal
No, but replace them with blank pages
quiz.why: Withdrawal is a request in a letter. Deleting leaves would rewrite the record of what was filed and makes a later refiling harder.

quiz.q: What does withdrawing an unapproved application mean for a later refiling?
options: It is without prejudice to refiling
It can be refiled only after 5 years
quiz.why: The regulations say withdrawal of an unapproved application is without prejudice to refiling.

steps: Create 0001 for the original application with sub-type amendment.
Add a cover letter (1.2) and Form FDA 356h (1.1).
Place the withdrawal request in the heading for withdrawal of an unapproved application.
Send nothing else, and no delete operations. Answer the quiz, validate and publish 0001.
hints: 1.5.7 is for withdrawing an approval that has been granted. This application was never approved.

missions.title: Initial IND
missions.brief: Before any phase 3 data exist, Ostrevia (lumiravostat) needs an IND so the first-in-human study can start in the US. Build the initial IND: the IND forms, the general investigational plan, the investigator's brochure, the CMC and toxicology data available now, and the phase 1 protocol with its study tagging file.

quiz.q: When may the first-in-human study start after the IND is sent?
options: 30 days after FDA receives the IND, unless FDA places a clinical hold or says it may start sooner
Only after FDA writes to approve it
quiz.why: An IND goes into effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA notifies the sponsor of a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA says so (21 CFR 312.40(b)).

quiz.q: Who signs Form FDA 1572?
quiz.why: Form FDA 1572 is the statement of investigator: each investigator commits to follow the protocol and the IND regulations.

quiz.q: Which study tagging file tag does the protocol carry?
quiz.why: Protocols and their amendments are tagged protocol-or-amendment; the report comes later with study-report.

steps: In Module 1, enter the IND number (six digits).
Place Forms FDA 1571, 1572 and 3674 in 1.1, and add a cover letter in 1.2.
Place the introductory statement and general investigational plan in 1.20 and the investigator's brochure in 1.14.4.1.
Add the CMC sections and the nonclinical study reports available now.
Place the HRP-101 protocol in 5.3.3.1 and tag it (Tag studies from documents).
Leave out anything that belongs to a marketing application. Answer the quiz, validate and publish 0000.
hints: An IND has its own form. The marketing application form is a trap here.
Modules 2 summaries are not required for an IND; the investigator's brochure carries the summary.

checks.label: IND number and US metadata complete

missions.title: 505(b)(2) application
missions.brief: Calderon Therapeutics has reformulated talmisartan as a once-daily extended-release capsule, Talvera XR. Instead of repeating every study, the NDA relies on FDA's finding for the listed drug Corvenza and on published literature, bridged by a relative bioavailability study. Build it, certify to the listed drug's patents, and leave out what you have no right to use.

quiz.q: What lets a 505(b)(2) application rely on information it did not generate?
options: A licence from the listed drug's holder is always required
The statute allows reliance on investigations not conducted by or for the applicant and to which it has no right of reference, such as literature or FDA's finding for a listed drug
Nothing: every study must be repeated
quiz.why: Section 505(b)(2) of the FD&C Act covers applications whose full reports of safety and effectiveness come at least partly from studies the applicant did not conduct and has no right of reference to.

quiz.q: Talvera XR certifies under Paragraph IV that a listed method-of-use patent is invalid or not infringed. What must follow?
options: Notice to the patent owner and to the listed drug's NDA holder
quiz.why: A Paragraph IV certification triggers notice to the patent owner and the NDA holder, which can start patent litigation and a 30-month stay.

quiz.q: If the relative bioavailability and clinical studies are essential to approval, what exclusivity could Talvera XR get?
quiz.why: Talmisartan is not a new chemical entity, but new clinical investigations essential to approval can earn 3 years of exclusivity for the change.

steps: In Module 1, enter the application number.
Build 0000 with the 505(b)(2) Module 1: forms, certifications, the patent certification for Corvenza in 1.3.5.2, the exclusivity claim and the draft labeling.
Place the scientific bridge: the clinical overview, the relative bioavailability and food-effect studies in 5.3.1.2, and the literature in 4.3 and 5.4.
Leave out anything you have no right to use.
Answer the quiz, validate and publish 0000.
hints: The patent certification is about the listed drug's patents; the patent information form (3542a) is about Talvera XR's own.
A study report from another company's NDA is not literature.

checks.label: Patent certification for the listed drug in 1.3.5.2
No reports you have no right of reference to

missions.title: Type II DMF and a letter of authorization
missions.brief: You work for Corvane Fine Chemicals, which makes the drug substance lumiravostat for Halcyon Ridge. Corvane keeps its process confidential, so it files its own Type II DMF. Build the DMF, then authorize Halcyon Ridge to reference it in their NDA.

quiz.q: Does FDA approve a DMF?
options: No: FDA reviews it only when an application references it
quiz.why: DMFs are neither approved nor disapproved. FDA reviews the technical content when it reviews an application that references the DMF.

quiz.q: What does a Type II DMF cover?
options: Drug substance, drug substance intermediates and materials used in their preparation, or drug product
quiz.why: Type II covers drug substance, intermediates and materials used in their preparation, or drug product. Type III is packaging; Type IV excipients; Type V other.

quiz.q: Who sends the letter of authorization to the DMF?
quiz.why: The holder authorizes a named customer to reference the DMF by filing a letter of authorization in its DMF (1.4.1), and gives the customer a copy for its application.

steps: In Module 1, check the holder (Corvane) and enter the DMF number (six digits).
Build 0000: Form FDA 3938 in 1.1, a cover letter with the statement of commitment in 1.2, the quality overall summary for the drug substance in 2.3, and 3.2.S.
Answer the quiz, validate and publish 0000.
Create 0001 as an amendment: cover letter, Form FDA 3938, and the letter of authorization for Halcyon Ridge in 1.4.1. Send nothing else. Validate and publish 0001.
hints: A DMF has no drug product: Module 3.2.P belongs to the customer's NDA.
The letter of authorization arrives in the library when you start 0001.

checks.label: DMF number and holder metadata complete
0000: quality overall summary for the drug substance in 2.3

missions.title: Decentralised procedure
missions.brief: Halcyon Ridge files Ostrevia through the decentralised procedure instead of the centralised one: the Netherlands as reference member state, with Germany, France and Ireland as concerned member states. The procedure number is NL/H/1234/001-002/DC. Set up the envelopes, give every member state its own product information in its own folder and language, and keep the centralised material out.

quiz.q: What distinguishes the decentralised procedure from mutual recognition?
options: In DCP no member state has authorised the product yet; in MRP the reference member state's existing authorisation is recognised by the others
quiz.why: DCP is for products not yet authorised anywhere in the EU; MRP extends an existing national authorisation to other member states.

quiz.q: After a positive end of the decentralised procedure, what happens?
options: The European Commission issues one decision
Each member state grants its own national authorisation within 30 days
quiz.why: DCP and MRP end in national authorisations, granted by each member state within 30 days of the agreement.

quiz.q: How many envelopes does the eu-regional.xml carry for this sequence?
options: One per receiving member state: four
quiz.why: Outside the centralised procedure each receiving member state gets an envelope with its country code; 'common' is not allowed in the envelope.

steps: In Module 1, enter the procedure number NL/H/1234/001-002/DC, choose the Netherlands as RMS and tick Germany, France and Ireland as CMSs.
Build 0000: cover letter, application form, Modules 2 to 5, and the rest of Module 1.
In 1.3.1, place the product information for each of the four member states. Look at the folders: country, then language.
Leave out the centralised product information in the 'ema' folder.
Answer the quiz, validate and publish 0000. Look at the four envelopes in eu-regional.xml.
hints: Ireland's product information is in English; the Netherlands', in Dutch.
The library's EMA product information is a trap here.

checks.label: Decentralised procedure, RMS Netherlands, CMS Germany, France and Ireland
Procedure number in the DCP format
One envelope per receiving member state
Product information for all four member states in 1.3.1

missions.title: Active substance master file
missions.brief: Corvane Fine Chemicals supplies lumiravostat to Halcyon Ridge for its EU marketing authorisation, but keeps its route of synthesis confidential. File an ASMF: one eCTD sequence in which 2.3.S and 3.2.S split into the applicant's part, which Halcyon Ridge may see, and the restricted part, for the authorities only.

quiz.q: Who sees the restricted part of an ASMF?
quiz.why: The restricted part holds confidential know-how and goes only to the authorities; the applicant's part is shared with the MA applicant.

quiz.q: What does the letter of access do?
options: Lets the ASMF holder see the MAA
Authorises the competent authorities to refer to the ASMF when assessing a named applicant's marketing authorisation application
quiz.why: The letter of access names the MA applicant and lets the authorities use the ASMF in that application's assessment.

quiz.q: How does the ASMF eCTD guideline tell AP and RP apart?
options: 'AP' or 'RP' in the substance attribute and in every leaf title of 2.3.S and 3.2.S, with -ap/-rp recommended in file names
quiz.why: One sequence, two branches of 2.3.S and 3.2.S, each marked AP or RP.

steps: In Module 1, enter the ASMF number EMEA/ASMF/01234 and check the holder (Corvane).
Build 0000 (submission type asmf, unit initial): a cover letter with the letter of access as an annex, and the quality expert information in 1.4.1.
Place the AP and RP quality overall summaries in 2.3.

Place 3.2.S: general information, characterisation, controls, reference standards, container and stability in the AP; the detailed manufacture (materials, critical steps, validation, development) in the RP. 3.2.S.2.2 and 3.2.S.3.2 have both an outline (AP) and a detailed (RP) version.
Keep restricted detail out of the applicant's part. Answer the quiz, validate and publish.
hints: Watch for a 3.2.S.2.3 document labelled AP: control of materials is restricted.
Look at the folder tree: the substance folder appears twice, once ending -ap and once -rp.

checks.label: ASMF number and holder metadata complete
Cover letter and quality expert information
AP and RP quality overall summaries in 2.3
No restricted information in the applicant's part
Every 2.3 and 3.2.S leaf marked AP or RP
